avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, fighting the emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: The City buys trees and has them planted on public land, and pays an organization to green private and institutional sites. Boroughs add their own resources: park fund money, equipment rental, blue-collar worker teams. Variances also govern tree planting in two building projects.

etapes.texte: City council awards contracts to 7574479 Canada inc. and to Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. to supply and plant 1,374 trees, then water them, maintain them and replace some of them. The maximum expenditure is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, for trees spread across seven boroughs.

Pierrefonds-Roxboro transfers up to $162,233.12 from its fund reserved for park purposes toward the purchase of trees and plants. City council pays $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an addition at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening instead of the 40 trees and 25% required. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger, for a two-storey building.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini-backhoe with operator for $152,916.75, taxes included, and sets aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar worker teams assigned to planting, from May to November 2026. Outremont entrusts URBEX Construction inc. with renovating the chalet in parc Pratt and redeveloping its surroundings, including planting vegetation, partly financed by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

City council leases land in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for a total rent of $100 before taxes. The organization stores materials, equipment and trees for planting there.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit its accountability report by December 31, 2026, at the latest, then its report and financial statements by March 31, 2027.
The lease for the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood nursery runs until April 30, 2028.

deneigement.description: Snow removal and snow loading contracts, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.

etapes.texte: Boroughs are renting vacuum sweepers, tanker trucks, sidewalk washers and a mini sweeper with operators to remove abrasives and clean streets, sidewalks and bike paths. In Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, the contract for cleaning sidewalks in four private snow removal sectors is awarded to Les Équipements Benco Canada ltée for $271,979.11, taxes included [CA26 27 0034].

etapes.titre: Maintenance and snow removal of public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie is awarding companies contracts for snow removal, spreading of abrasives and maintenance of downtown public squares, including Square Viger, Place des Montréalaises, square Dorchester and square Victoria. The borough is also extending snow removal for the Quartier des Spectacles by one year, from April 2, 2026 to April 1, 2027 [CA26 24 0067].

Montréal-Nord is paying $106,150.97 more for the rental of an additional grader [CA26 10 086]. Saint-Léonard is drawing $200,000 from its surpluses to pay staff and buy salt and sand [CA26 13 0121]. Verdun is offering to have city council itself provide staff for its snow disposal site.

The City is extending turnkey snow removal contracts in Anjou, Montréal-Nord and Pierrefonds-Roxboro by twelve months, as well as towing contracts in four boroughs and equipment rentals with operator in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie. Boroughs are doing the same for their own machine rentals.

aSurveiller.texte: The extended towing contracts for Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, Ville-Marie and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension start on November 15, 2026.
The eight turnkey snow removal contracts awarded in August cover four winter seasons and end on April 15, 2030.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: The City is funding and building the disinfection unit at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, and is awarding several maintenance and upgrade contracts for this plant. It is also having water and sewer pipes rehabilitated or rebuilt in many boroughs, with the replacement of lead service connections, on both the public and private sides. Loan by-laws govern the financing of this work.

etapes.titre: Lead water service connections taken on by boroughs
etapes.texte: Lachine, Le Sud-Ouest and Ahuntsic-Cartierville are offering city council to carry out themselves the replacement of lead service connections located on private land, under by-law 20-030. The costs of work done on private property are billed to owners.

etapes.titre: New loans and addition to an ongoing contract
etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council adopts a $12,000,000 loan for main pipes in the Namur–De la Savane sector. It adds $12,144,522.14 in contingencies to Pomerleau's contract for the rue de la Cathédrale pipe, toward the McTavish reservoir, after an inspection revealed more damaged sections than in 2019.

aSurveiller.texte: Adoption planned for October 19, 2026 of the $951,000,000 loan by-law for the renewal of secondary waterworks and sewer networks.
Commissioning of the ozone plant planned for 2029; the contracts for lots 4, 5 and 6 must end in the last quarter of 2028.
Shutdown of sludge incinerator 2 starting the first week of October 2026 and of incinerator 4 in January 2027, about six weeks each.
Rehabilitation of the 600 mm pipe along autoroute 15 Nord and the Atwater ramp to be completed no later than December 18, 2026.
Completion of the rue de la Cathédrale pipe work postponed from December 2026 to March 2027.

frederic-back.titre: Parc Frédéric-Back and Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned landfill, transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, electrical upgrades.
frederic-back.enBref: This year, the City is moving forward on three fronts at parc Frédéric-Back: a greenhouse complex in the southwest sector of the park, the upgrade of electrical installations at the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel, and the park's regular maintenance. It also requested funding from Québec for a trail crossing the park from east to west, and launched the redevelopment of rue De Louvain along the edge of the park.

etapes.titre: Funding request for an east-west link
etapes.texte: The City is asking the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec for funding of up to $2,000,000 for a 900-metre multi-use trail crossing the park from east to west, with a footbridge of about 150 metres. The project also includes stormwater management works and a 12.7-hectare meadow [CG26 0121].

etapes.titre: Green light for the greenhouse project
etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration approves the construction of a greenhouse complex near the composting platform: 1,500 m² for research and training, 1,000 m² for the Saint-Michel neighbourhood's community greenhouse, with a construction budget estimated at $2,185,000 [CG26 0124]. The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offers to carry out the project, and city council accepts.

The City awards Systèmes Urbains inc. the second phase of electrical work at the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel, for $1,091,693.37 taxes included: a new 25 kV power supply, transformer, backup generator and automated controller to manage biogas capture [CG26 0223]. It also awards Groupe Nicky and Les Entreprises Roseneige the general maintenance and ecological and horticultural management of the park, from May 1, 2026 to October 31, 2028 [CG26 0224].

The borough awards Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue De Louvain, between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82 taxes included. The work covers sewers and water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings, in three phases from 2026 to 2028.

The City is extending by five months the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor with operator, from June 20 to October 15, 2026, for an additional expense of $296,349.21 taxes included. The compost is used as a soil amendment, notably for the development of parc Frédéric-Back [CG26 0320].

aSurveiller.texte: The call for projects under the ministère des Transports' funding program, for the footbridge and the east-west link, closes on November 26, 2026.
Installation work on the greenhouses must be completed by December 2026, with commissioning announced for winter 2027.
26 more hectares will be added to the park in 2027, in the Boisé Ouest sector.
Work on rue De Louvain continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, bump-outs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
The park maintenance contracts run until October 31, 2028, with two possible 12-month extensions.

grand-parc-ouest.description: Canada's largest municipal park, being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.

etapes.texte: The City added $162,897.98, taxes included, to the contract for the repair of the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77. According to the file, buried stones requiring hand-cleaning, a larger quantity of mortar and a deteriorated culvert explain the increase.

The City authorized the submission of the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector, described as covering 330 hectares, for the international Urban Night Sky Place designation from DarkSky International. The application requires no financial commitment; the City commits to producing a lighting management plan and bringing its light fixtures up to standard.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as protected areas
etapes.texte: The City listed the parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector (429 ha) in the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité, with conservation plans providing for ecological management. It also took note of the 2025 report on surface areas.

The City awarded Gendron Gestion Civil inc. a contract to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, as part of the modernization of the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub, for a total expenditure of $481,850.45, taxes included. The culvert had been damaged by the heavy rains of August 2024.

aSurveiller.texte: The Cap-Saint-Jacques lighting management plan must be submitted in February 2027, DarkSky International's response is expected in April 2027, and full compliance for the site is set for April 2032.
The snow removal contract covers two winters, from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028, with no possible extension.
The janitorial services contract for the nine Cap-Saint-Jacques buildings runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2030, with an option to extend until October 31, 2031.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: The City lends municipal buildings to organizations to open warming centres, and it funds organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness. It also deploys a Ville-Marie public works team to other boroughs for cleanliness interventions related to homelessness. It is setting up a framework for receiving private donations and is appealing a ruling on the encampments under the Van Horne viaduct.

etapes.texte: The City lends three buildings free of charge to organizations for the winter: the church at 5600, 12e Avenue to the Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal, the former monastery of the Recluses Missionnaires at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est to Projets Autochtones du Québec, and the Bain St-Denis at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN. The loans end on April 30, 2026 and the value of the unbilled rent is estimated at $57,076 for the church.

Verdun pays $12,950 to the Société de développement social to keep outreach workers in its municipal facilities from January 5 to February 6, 2026. Ahuntsic-Cartierville ratifies the continuation of the contract with Les services de cohabitation sociale COHAB inc. for a warming centre for winter 2025-2026.

The City grants financial support to community organizations under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs 2026-2028, for inclusion, public space cohabitation and awareness projects. The amounts cover a three-year period ending December 31, 2028.

etapes.titre: Private donations and Bain St-Denis setup
etapes.texte: City council adopts a framework for receiving private donations intended for housing, shelter and social cohabitation projects; donors do not choose which project is funded. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie transfers $250,000 for the activities and setup work of the temporary warming centre at the Bain Saint-Denis. City council also adopts a declaration of support for people experiencing homelessness and a motion on a rent support fund.

etapes.titre: Encampments on rue Notre-Dame and appeal of the ruling
etapes.texte: The City awards a contract worth $149,520, taxes included, to Mission Old Brewery to support people from the rue Notre-Dame encampment area toward shelter and housing, and pays $90,000 to the Réseau d'aide aux personnes seules et itinérantes de Montréal for the 2026, 2027 and 2028 editions of the Nuit des sans-abri. The executive committee takes charge of the litigation over the encampments under the Van Horne viaduct and authorizes an appeal of the June 8, 2026 ruling.

aSurveiller.texte: Mission Old Brewery's mandate in the rue Notre-Dame encampment area ends on October 18, 2026.
The agreement between Ville-Marie and Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for the public works team runs until May 15, 2027.
Support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs ends on December 31, 2028.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood being built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary developments.

etapes.texte: The City is extending the lease of a piece of land to the Société de transport de Montréal for parking vehicles used by its agents, south of rue de Louvain and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent. It is also extending the lease of a neighbouring piece of land to a company for paid parking reserved for members of an application.

The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough is awarding a company the redevelopment of rue de Louvain, between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel. The work involves sewers, water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

etapes.titre: Main street becomes avenue des Solidarités
etapes.texte: City council is naming the new street at the heart of the eco-district "avenue des Solidarités." The name comes from a public call for proposals held in fall 2024.

The City is awarding a contract to build a road with sewer, water main, roadworks, electrical network and lighting in the eco-district, as well as for environmental management of the soil. It is adding $2,007,312.15 net, from the environmental liability reserve, to rehabilitate the soil of the former gas station area on the Louvain Est site.

The borough is adopting a draft resolution authorizing the demolition of a building on avenue de l'Esplanade and rue de Louvain Ouest, then the construction of a group of buildings with a minimum density of 200 dwelling units per hectare. It is also launching a draft by-law to increase the height and density allowed on part of the municipal land at 50 and 150, rue de Louvain Ouest.

aSurveiller.texte: The lease of the land rented to the Société de transport de Montréal for parking starts on October 1, 2026, for three years, at a rate of 92 days per year.
The free loan of the land for planting sunflowers and the greenhouse runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027.
The free loan of the land for the community garden continues until December 31, 2027.
The land at the corner of rue de Louvain Ouest and avenue de l'Esplanade would be loaned for programming activities from April 1 to October 31, 2027.

Work on rue de Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, bump-outs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
The street naming file indicates that site developments are planned for around 2032 and that four other public places still need to be named.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack: sale of land, loan by-laws, water main for the Namur–De la Savane area.
namur-hippodrome.enBref: This year, the City is preparing the ground, both literally and financially, for the future neighbourhood on the site of the former racetrack. It obtained more time from the Québec government to sell a first parcel of land, guaranteed a loan meant for studies, and adopted two loan by-laws for streets, sewers and the water main in the area. At the same time, it is leasing parcels of the site to organizations for temporary uses.

etapes.titre: More time to sell a first parcel of land
etapes.texte: The Québec government grants the City a deadline until October 31, 2027 to sell a first parcel of land on the site, located west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. According to the file, the postponement does not involve any financial compensation and the other conditions of the 2017 transfer deed remain the same.

City council approves a $2,000,000 City guarantee in favour of the Canada Infrastructure Bank, for a loan to the organization GALOPH that will be used to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. On the same day, council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on governance and asset management in the development of the neighbourhood.

The City adopts a $29,000,000 loan to develop the neighbourhood's public domain: soil remediation, sewers and water main, street redevelopment, fees and land purchases. It also adopts a $12,000,000 loan to build water main pipes between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.

etapes.titre: Project for four buildings on rue Namur
etapes.texte: The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopts a draft resolution authorizing the construction of four buildings, in four phases, at 7301 boulevard Décarie and 5150-5160 rue Namur, one of which is to house a municipal sports and recreation centre. The developer will pay $3,200,000 for public amenities and facilities in the area, and a public consultation meeting will be held.

aSurveiller.texte: The sale of a first parcel of land must be completed no later than October 31, 2027.
The federal grant is conditional on the infrastructure being completed by 2031.
The temporary leases end on April 30, 2027 (MultiCaf), March 31, 2028 (Polliflora) and April 30, 2028 (transitional nursery).

parcs.description: Development and renovation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: This year, the City is funding park renovations across the island: new play areas, water play areas, dog parks, trails and plantings. It is also awarding contracts in the Grand parc de l'Ouest, submitting the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector's candidacy for an international dark sky designation, and adding two natural environments to a protection registry. Several decisions adjust contracts for construction already underway.

etapes.texte: The City awards the winning team of an architecture competition the design of the bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and the redevelopment of parc Le Prévost, for a total expense of $10,559,257.81, taxes included. It also provides funding to Verdun for soil studies at parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard and launches a public art competition for the parc des Eaux-Cachées, in Griffintown.

Several decisions add amounts to or shift budgets within already awarded contracts: construction monitoring at parc du Bassin-à-Bois, parc des Hirondelles and parc du Sault-au-Récollet in Ahuntsic-Cartierville, parc Villeray, and professional services at parc Percy-Walters. The City also provides $168,472.14 to Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension to decontaminate parc George-Vernot.

City council removes a 810.2 m² street segment from the public domain to add it to parc Campbell Ouest, in Côte-Saint-Paul. Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension requests the same change for a 75.2 m² strip of lane that crosses parc Le Prévost.

aSurveiller.texte: Executive committee on October 7, 2026 and city council on October 19, 2026 on the lane strip at parc Le Prévost.
Selection of the winning project for the parc des Eaux-Cachées public art competition in October 2026, contract in December 2026 and installation of the artwork in 2028.
Start of the Grand parc de l'Ouest snow removal contract on November 1, 2026, until April 30, 2028.
Janitorial maintenance of nine Cap-Saint-Jacques buildings from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2030.
End of work at parc Denise-Morelle in November 2026.
Work at parc Percy-Walters from July to November 2026, with a continuation in spring 2027.
Work at parc J.O.R.-Leduc until June 2028.
Response from DarkSky International expected in April 2027; lighting plan submitted in February 2027 and site compliance in April 2032.
Final acceptance of work at parc du Bassin-à-Bois expected in June 2027.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and business animation ordinances.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City is funding and overseeing temporary pedestrian streets on commercial arteries, mainly for the 2026 summer season. The executive committee paid $2,694,500 to the boroughs under the call for projects for pedestrianization on commercial arteries [CE26 0465], and the boroughs adopted the ordinances that close the streets, and authorize terraces, sales and music. Other decisions concern public squares: landscaping, change of status of a lot, and an official name.

etapes.titre: Grant rules and settlement of a dispute
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law that allows it to subsidize its business development corporations to pedestrianize streets, up to $425 per linear metre, provided council closes the street by ordinance [CA26 240037]. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie settles out of court for $41,686.46 a lawsuit related to work on the public square at the corner of rues Beaubien Est and Boyer [CA26 26 0010].

The executive committee distributes $2,694,500 among boroughs for pedestrian streets closed for at least eight consecutive weeks, including rue Villeray as a new project [CE26 0465]. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce creates the Placette CDN from April 1 to October 31, 2026 [CA26 170058] and Ville-Marie bans traffic on the sections of its summer pedestrianizations [CA26 240090].

The boroughs pay contributions to the business development corporations that organize the pedestrian streets: $102,045 for rue Villeray [CA26 14 0078], $375,500 for rue Sainte-Catherine Est [CA26 240134] and $67,500 for avenue Lacombe until 2028 [CA26 170108]. Outremont allocates $105,000 to the pedestrianization of avenue Bernard, in addition to a $106,000 grant from the Service du développement économique [CA26 16 0061].

Borough councils close their arteries to cars and regulate terraces, sales and noise: avenue Bernard from May 19 to September 24 [CA26 16 0082], avenues Royal and Madison from June 1 to October 31 [CA26 170088], rue Ontario Est from June 15 to September 18 [CA26 27 0115], avenues du Mont-Royal and Duluth [CA26 25 0134]. Ville-Marie adjusts the dates of three pedestrianizations [CA26 240155] and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve removes 113 paid parking spaces [CA26 27 0119].

etapes.titre: Public squares and end of season
etapes.texte: City council changes a 899-square-metre lot at the corner of rue Sherbrooke Est and boulevard Langelier from street (public square) status to local park status [CM26 0888] and names the public square at the corner of rue Charleroi and avenue L'Archevêque "place Chez-Marguerite" [CM26 0913]. Ville-Marie authorizes sound ambiance on the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles [CA26 240372] and Le Plateau-Mont-Royal revises the reopening schedule for avenue du Mont-Royal [CA26 25 227].

aSurveiller.texte: Avenue du Mont-Royal reopens to traffic between Saint-Denis and Resther on September 30, 2026, and between Saint-Laurent and Saint-Denis on October 15, 2026.
Boroughs must report on the amounts received for pedestrianizations in November 2026 and return unspent money in December 2026.
The ordinance on sound ambiance for the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles runs until September 2, 2027.
The on-demand transit contract on avenue du Mont-Royal covers until December 31, 2027, and support for the pedestrianization of avenue Lacombe until December 31, 2028.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws that each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville amends its urban planning by-law for the planting, maintenance, protection and felling of trees. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie revises its urban planning, special projects and demolition by-laws, and Saint-Léonard does the same for its special projects and demolitions, following public consultations held on February 26 and February 11, 2026.

The borough extends its list of buildings of heritage interest, regulates establishments providing housing and services for people experiencing residential instability, and amends its by-laws on demolition, special projects, and site planning and architectural integration programs. A public assembly was held on March 18, 2026, and a written consultation took place from March 11 to 18, 2026.

The borough changes the heights, uses and site coverage ratio in the sector bounded by avenue Papineau, avenue Émile-Journault, avenue André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est. It also increases the permitted heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse, between boulevard Crémazie and boulevard Henri-Bourassa.

etapes.titre: Requests for extensions to the ministry
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève requests six more months, citing staff shortages, the complexity of its territory and the fall 2025 election.

Ville-Marie amends its urban planning by-law and its by-laws on special projects, demolition, authorization certificates and cadastral operations. After the public consultation of March 25, 2026, the City revised the view corridor and height plans; the by-law allows a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and requires approval for certain work in the declared heritage site of Mont-Royal.

Saint-Léonard takes note of two correction minutes signed on March 19, 2026, which correct the name of a school and the identification of a building on boulevard Provencher. Ahuntsic-Cartierville then adopts its by-law on the demolition of buildings, following a public consultation assembly held on June 23, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève states it wants to present its project to elected officials starting mid-June 2026 and hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.

The Minister of Municipal Affairs has set June 16, 2027, as the deadline for Saint-Léonard to adopt all its concordance by-laws; other blocks are announced, including the replacement of the zoning by-law.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests an extension until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027, to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.

securite-publique.description: The Service de police de la Ville de Montréal: contracts, neighbourhood stations, council motions.

etapes.titre: Loan for equipment and loan of a police officer
etapes.texte: The City adopts a by-law authorizing a loan of $10,880,000 to buy and replace specialized public safety equipment between 2026 and 2030. It also authorizes the loan of a detective sergeant to the RCMP team on enforcement of the Firearms Act, starting January 7, 2026.

The City buys patrol motorcycles, extends the headquarters' housekeeping contract by one year, and awards a contract to replace the oil heating system of the cavalry building, at 1515 chemin Remembrance. It authorizes a second loan of a police officer to the RCMP, starting March 30, 2026, with an additional budget of $136,260 for 2026.

etapes.titre: Meals for detainees and call-handling software
etapes.texte: The City awards a company the preparation and delivery of meals for people detained by the SPVM, for three years. It also extends by twelve months the maintenance of the patrol and emergency call dispatch software, and accepts a $8,000 federal grant for a sexual assault awareness campaign.

etapes.titre: Motions of support after the shooting
etapes.texte: After the shooting on June 22, 2026 in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, borough councils adopt motions of support for the SPVM. They offer condolences to the families and reaffirm their commitment to the police service.

aSurveiller.texte: Secondment agreement for police officers to the RCMP's Integrated Synthetic Drug Enforcement Team, starting October 12, 2026, for three years.
"Fèves au lard" day at neighbourhood station 46, on October 23, 2026, for which the Anjou borough buys tickets.
Start of the lease for the metro unit of neighbourhood station 50, at 888 boulevard De Maisonneuve Est, on February 1, 2027.
Delivery of the port patrol boat and its trailer no later than March 1, 2027.
End of the heating replacement work at the cavalry building, expected September 30, 2027.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides around the network: land sold to the STM, areas around stations, agreements.

etapes.texte: The City is selling a 364.3 square metre plot of land for $495,150 to expand the Place-Saint-Henri station entrance building, land in Verdun for $257,425 to rebuild and expand the Rielle ventilation plant, and is committing to sell a plot of about 202.8 square metres on rue Jean-Brillant for $115,000 to build a rectifier station there. These amounts are shown before applicable taxes.

Elected officials approve several STM loan by-laws and the corresponding amendments to the 2026-2035 capital works program. They cover reserved bus lanes and priority traffic lights for buses, the repair of metro and surface infrastructure, cybersecurity, extending the service life of the MR-73 cars and analyzing their replacement.

The City is buying advertising space in the STM network and with Astral for Espace pour la vie, for a maximum of $172,462.50, taxes included, and is granting $382,000 to the STM to strengthen service during the 2026 UCI Road World Championships. The executive committee accepts on loan the archaeological collection from the REM excavations; councils adopt motions on preserving the blue line tunnel boring machine and on a structuring public transit project in the east end.

aSurveiller.texte: The Ahuntsic-Cartierville parking lease begins on October 1, 2026, for three years, for a maximum of 92 days per year.
Work on the Rielle ventilation plant, in Verdun, is to continue until December 2027.
Rue Wilderton will be closed for a maximum of two weeks during the 2027 summer vacation period, for the reconstruction of the bridge-tunnel; work is scheduled until March 2028.
The opening of the five new blue line stations is planned for 2031; the City's work there is integrated in 2028-2029.

velo.titre: Bike: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and bike lanes, and the self-service bike system.

etapes.texte: Outremont approved spending of $100,000, taxes included, for concrete, de-icing salt and abrasives used in particular on bike paths. Ahuntsic-Cartierville awarded a contract worth $153,395.05, taxes included, for the rental of a mini sweeper with operator that cleans paths less than 1.8 metres wide in the spring.

etapes.titre: BIXI bikes and sustainable mobility corridors
etapes.texte: City council awarded a sole-source contract worth $4,815,802.61, taxes included, to PBSC Solutions Urbaines inc. for mechanical bikes, electric-assist bikes, stations and docking points compatible with BIXI. It also added $3,400,000, taxes included, to the contract of Bruneau Électrique inc. for lights, civil and electrical work, and bike paths in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve.

City council approved an agreement worth $125,167.62, taxes included, to pay Hydro-Québec the 2014 to 2025 rent for land used for bike paths, parks and community gardens. It then approved a 10-year lease, starting January 1, 2026, for a parcel of about 366 square metres in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, with total rent of $46,896, taxes included.

etapes.titre: Repairs to REV Lajeunesse and avenue Lajoie
etapes.texte: Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offered to take charge of repairing sections of the REV Lajeunesse, between rue Jarry and boulevard Crémazie, and city council accepted this offer as well as Ville-Marie's offer for roadway and bike lane work. Outremont gave a notice of motion to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie, between Stuart and Outremont, into a one-way bike path.

aSurveiller.texte: The UCI Road World Championships will be held in Montréal from September 20 to 27, 2026; roadway work is planned along the route in Ville-Marie.
Complete financial assistance applications for the rue de Champlain, Saint-Jacques, Guy and Laurier projects must be submitted no later than October 9, 2026.
